claims.text: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a single-phase BCC microstructure.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a room-temperature yield strength of approximately 1600 MPa.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a yield strength of approximately 855 MPa at 1000 °C.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of approximately 10.21 g/cm³.
Replacing part of Hf with Sc will reduce the density of HfMoTaTiZr.
Sc has a density of 2.985 g/cm³.
Limited Sc substitution in HfMoTaTiZr will retain a predominantly BCC primary matrix.
Sc substitution may generate a fine dispersion of Sc-containing precipitates.
Sc can occur as a minor second phase within a dominant BCC matrix.
A controlled BCC-plus-precipitate microstructure will provide precipitation strengthening.
The BCC matrix is responsible for maintaining ductile, high-strength performance at room temperature and 1000 °C.
The Sc-modified alloy will have a density 5–10% below that of as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
The Sc-modified alloy will retain room-temperature yield strength within approximately 10% of 1600 MPa.
The Sc-modified alloy will retain yield strength at 1000 °C within approximately 10% of 855 MPa.
Extensive formation of intermetallic or non-BCC phases would compromise the predicted mechanical performance.
Approximately 10 atomic % Sc can be introduced by replacing Hf while retaining the desired microstructure and strengths.

contradictions.description: The formula Hf(0.9-x)Sc(x)MoTaTiZr is inconsistent with the stated approximately 10 atomic % Sc substitution. For example, x = 0.1 gives only about 2 atomic % Sc after normalization and also reduces the Hf coefficient from 0.9 rather than from the equiatomic value 1.

The hypothesis frames Sc substitution into an as-cast baseline as the single intervention, but the modified alloy is to undergo homogenization and unspecified thermal treatments. This produces a different processing state from the as-cast comparator and confounds substitution with heat treatment.
